first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A company that plans weddings in Portugal and will put us in touch with one advisor. The headline is about palaces and cliffs, which sounds gorgeous but big. The good bit is right under it: a quick answer that says foreign couples can marry legally there with about a month's notice, and a little bar where I can pick 'under 30' guests and 'elopement'. That bar is what keeps me on the page.

attention_map.quote: Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff
attention_map.why: Pretty, but a palace makes me picture 150 people and a ballroom. The legal quick answer ('organised at least one month before the date') and 'Check the rules for your passport' is what actually hooks me, because paperwork is my biggest worry.

attention_map.quote: include an 'under 30' band for the elopement persona; What are you celebrating? Wedding, elopement...
attention_map.why: First sign that a tiny group is welcome. Seeing 'elopement' as a choice and a guest band that fits us is exactly what I scan for on my phone. It is only a form bar though, not a promise anyone wants us.

attention_map.quote: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor
attention_map.why: Fine, one person looking after us is reassuring, but nothing to stop for.

attention_map.quote: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.why: Pena, Monserrate, UNESCO Douro. Lovely photos probably, but I am scrolling past to find guest numbers and minimums.

An airport on every region card is genuinely useful because we want to keep it simple and close to a flight. But the Guests line is left out or says 'Ask your Wedded Advisor', so I still do not know if a venue will take six of us.

attention_map.quote: events on those dates may have to be cancelled
attention_map.why: Honest, I like that, but it makes a palace sound like more hassle than a small group needs.

attention_map.quote: a Catholic marriage is legally recognised on its own
attention_map.why: This is a real answer to one of my questions. Plain and clear.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; ... fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum
attention_map.why: This is the exact thing I fear: a minimum built for a big group. It tells me minimums exist but not what they are, so for a group of ten it reads like 'you might pay for empty rooms'.

attention_map.quote: witnesses may take part but are not mandatory
attention_map.why: Best part of the page for me. Documents listed, the Registo Civil named, one month minimum, official links, and witnesses not required, which matters when it is only close family. Numbered 4 steps is what I need when I do not know where to start.

attention_map.quote: for about 100 guests: total EUR 25,000 to 70,000
attention_map.why: Everything shown at 100-guest scale. The under-30 band is not shown, so I have no idea what our size costs. If the figures are hidden until sign-off, there are no numbers at all, which feels like minimums hidden until the call.

attention_map.quote: Venue nights with rooms, welcome dinner, ceremony, long dinner, late party, Sunday brunch
attention_map.why: This is a big production. We do not want a three-day party. Nothing says what a small or elopement version looks like.

attention_map.quote: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.why: Transfers and guest websites are for bigger groups. Not for us.

attention_map.quote: ceremony type (legal in Portugal, Catholic, symbolic, not sure)
attention_map.why: The form asks guest count and legal or symbolic, so it feels like they will take my situation seriously. I still want it said that they will sort the documents for us.

attention_map.quote: Can Australian, US or UK citizens marry legally in Portugal?
attention_map.why: Short yes/no answers by passport. Useful. No FAQ about small weddings or minimum spend though.

questions_answered.question: Does this work for 30 guests or fewer, and is there a smaller package?
questions_answered.evidence: Only the qualifier bar's 'under 30' band and the 'elopement' option hint yes. Region cards have no guest line, there are no packages at all ('no package, a planned weekend instead'), and the weekend section describes a big party. Nothing says in words that small groups are welcome.

questions_answered.question: Do you handle the legal side: documents, witnesses, registry?
questions_answered.evidence: The rules are explained very well: Registo Civil, 'at least one month before the date', document list, 'witnesses may take part but are not mandatory', rules by passport with official sources. But I do not see a line saying the Wedded Advisor will gather or lodge the documents for us. Explained is not the same as handled.

questions_answered.question: What is the minimum spend?
questions_answered.evidence: Venue charges box says 'fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum' with no figure, the cost table is for 'about 100 guests' only, and it may be hidden until sign-off. No minimum for a small group anywhere.

questions_answered.question: Can we have a religious ceremony (for example Catholic) here?
questions_answered.evidence: 'a Catholic marriage is legally recognised on its own' plus 'civil marriage in religious form' for other faiths, and Catholic is a choice in the enquiry form.

objections_triggered.objection: Minimum guest numbers or spend that don't fit a small group
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms' and 'per guest with a minimum', with no figure and only a 100-guest cost band
H1 palace and cliff, 'late party, Sunday brunch' weekend, guest transfers, cost table for about 100 guests

Mostly calmed by the numbered 4 steps and official links; still some hedging for Australians ('Confirm with the Registo Civil or the Embassy of Portugal in Canberra which document you need') which leaves me to chase it myself

trust_signals_noticed: Clear legal steps with official sources (justica.gov.pt, smartraveller, gov.uk, US Embassy)
Nearest airport on every region card
One Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding
Honest palace rules, including the Monserrate scaffolding
turn_offs_noticed: Everything shown at big-group scale: 100-guest cost table, three-day weekend with a late party
Minimums mentioned but never stated, which feels like they come out on the call
No small or elopement option described anywhere except a form dropdown

emotional_response.relief: The legal section makes me feel I could actually do this without a lawyer.
emotional_response.unease: The rest of the page reads like it is for someone else's much bigger wedding.
emotional_response.overwhelm: Seven tabs and 2,400 plus words on a phone is a lot, though the tabs help.

payload.decision_reason: The legal side is the clearest I have seen and the Catholic question is answered, so I would not leave. But I only enquire if small groups are clearly welcome, and here the only sign is an 'under 30' option in a form while costs, the weekend and minimums are all pitched at big weddings. No minimum spend, and nothing says they will do the paperwork for us, so I save it and keep comparing.
payload.verbatim_reaction: OK, the legal bit is great, a month's notice, no witnesses needed, my documents listed, I actually get it now. But is this for us? It's palaces, a late party, Sunday brunch and costs for 100 people. There's a box saying I might pay for empty rooms with a minimum, but no number. We're maybe 12 people. I'd save this and come back, but I'm not filling in a form until I know a small group won't get stung with a minimum.
